Definition
A motor that drives a generator, changes electrical power to mechanical power, then mechanical power to electrical power.
Ideally power in and power out are equal but friction and resistance cause some power losses.
Due to losses, the percentage of motor generator efficiency needs to be calculated.
Power in, power out, losses and percent efficiency are all main concerns of motor generator users.
Let's begin the lesson on MOTOR GENERATORS................................
LESSON MENU
MOTOR GENERATOR ACTION
A generator converts mechanical energy to electrical energy.
DISCUSSION
A motor converts electrical energy to mechanical energy.
When a motor is used to drive a generator, energy is changed from electrical to mechanical and back to electrical.
Both the motor and the generator are actually energy conversion devices.
In a no loss condition, a motors input power (watts) is equal to the output power (watts).
Using a motor to drive a generator, input power is still equal to output power considering there are no losses in either the motor or generator.
You will find that power in does not equal power out due to losses in the motor generator.
How well a rotating device converts power is known as efficiency.
An inefficient system has high power loss.
An inefficient system has high power loss.
The value of percent efficiency is a systems power conversion capability.
For example, the efficiency of this motor generator set is 75%.
